purpose: Portable, tool-agnostic description of this workspace so any coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ...) can pick up the same skills, rules, and runbooks. Displayed at webapp.lan and referenceable by agents.

workspace.note: The working copy is E:\REPO\ptm4 on ptm (the Windows side of the workstation, local NTFS) since 2026-09-08; GitHub is the central copy. Edit there. opti holds only a .git-less deploy snapshot of homelab/ that opti-deploy.yml rsyncs on every push — never edit it. homelab/agentic/ is tracked in git except generated/ (written nightly on opti, pulled locally by probe.py --wire claude) and .claude/ (copies made by probe.py --wire claude), so nothing unique lives in either. Commit new rules/skills/hooks; uncommitted files exist only on disk.

access_paths.opti_deploy_snapshot: /srv/red/fs/ptm/repo/ptm4/homelab (rsync target, not git; read-only by convention)
access_paths.webapp_workspace_mount: /workspace in the webapp container = /srv/red/fs/ptm/repo/ptm4 on opti, read-only

current_agent.discovery_link_design: Real skill and rule content lives in agentic/skills/<name>/ and agentic/rules/; Claude Code only discovers them under .claude/, so `probe.py --wire claude` COPIES them there (no symlinks: they need admin or Developer Mode on NTFS) and prunes copies whose source was removed. It also rewrites the CLAUDE.md pointer block, merges the harness hooks into .claude/settings.json, and pulls opti's agentic/generated/*.md. Edit the agentic/ sources, then re-wire.

portability.summary: This workspace is described tool-agnostically. Skills are folders with a SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter: name + description, then a Markdown procedure). Rules are standing behavioral Markdown files. Runbooks are per-host/subsystem operational Markdown. Any agent can read these directly; only the *discovery* wiring differs per tool.
for_a_new_tool: Point the tool at homelab/agentic/ as the source of truth.
Load agentic/rules/*.md as always-on system rules.
Register each agentic/skills/<name> per the tool's skill/command mechanism.
Treat agentic/runbooks/*.md as retrievable reference docs.

tool_adapters.claude_code: probe.py --wire claude copies agentic/skills -> .claude/skills and agentic/rules -> .claude/rules (auto-loaded); CLAUDE.md points here
tool_adapters.codex: AGENTS.md points Codex at homelab/agentic; .codex/rules and .codex/skills hold copies (no automated wire in probe.py yet)
tool_adapters.cursor: TODO: reference agentic/rules from .cursor/rules; skills as callable commands

skills.name: add-to-webapp
skills.description: Add or change anything on the homelab dashboard — Pertal (webapp v4, https://webapp.lan:8444, becomes :8443 at cutover) — a page, tab, data source, button/action, Status card, resource or topology node, or API route. Use when the user asks to add/publish/show something on the web app, the dashboard, Pertal, webapp.lan, "Pert's Pocket" (the v3 name) or "the rpi web app" (old name — it runs on opti), or to change what the dashboard shows or does.

skills.name: add-webapp-widget
skills.description: Add a widget, card, tile or panel to the homelab dashboard — in Pertal (webapp v4, webapp.lan:8444) follow add-to-webapp's recipes; this file covers v3.Fable (webapp.lan:8443) fixes only — something showing live data, status, or a small feed on Home, the Monitor, the Control center, a host page, or the Launchpad. Use when the user asks for something to appear on the dashboard/board/home screen as a card or tile, or to add/change a dashboard widget.

skills.name: homelab-ssh
skills.description: SSH into a homelab server (opti, rpi, noblenumbat, or android) to run commands, check status, or make changes on that box. Use whenever a query names one of these hosts and doing anything about it requires actually logging in (not just reading about it in docs).

skills.name: modding-standards
skills.description: Standards for modding any PC game or app safely — backups and hash-guarded uninstaller before the first file lands, manifests, archiving mod binaries, version pinning, log-based verification, anti-cheat hard line. Use before installing, updating, fixing or removing any game mod, injector, ReShade/RenoDX addon, DLSS/upscaler swap, loose-file or plugin mod (Starfield, AC, etc.), or when un-modding an install.

skills.name: opti-drive-onboard
skills.description: Onboard a new physical drive into the opti server (192.168.1.11). Use when the user says they installed a new drive in opti or wants to expand opti storage. Since 2026-07-25 the live storage is ZFS pool `red` — a new drive is either a mirror for it (preferred) or a pool expansion, NOT a mergerfs branch.

skills.name: radarr-add
skills.description: Add movies to the homelab Radarr (noblenumbat) by title/year. Use when the user asks to add movies to Radarr, the media server, or their Jellyfin library. Handles lookup, year matching, duplicate detection, and triggers an automatic download search.

skills.name: sonarr-add
skills.description: Add TV series (including docuseries) to the homelab Sonarr (noblenumbat) by title/year. Use when the user asks to add shows, series, seasons, or multi-part documentaries to Sonarr, the media server, or their Jellyfin library.
